sample_source_detail.selection: units ordered by (source_run, task_id) so the first N units are one complete benchmark round; cells taken round-robin across units

tokenizer.how_resolved: tiktoken.get_encoding('cl100k_base') succeeded from the local tiktoken cache

approximation_error_vs_cl100k.note: the byte-class approximation is the LAST tier and is never used while a real tokenizer resolves; these are its residuals against the primary tokenizer on the shape panel, reported so the fallback's quality is visible rather than assumed

tokenizer.why_not_only_the_endpoint: the endpoint's usage.prompt_tokens is content-cached and intermittently inflated; it is used as a secondary cross-check, not as the primary measurement

endpoint_protocol.hazard: usage.prompt_tokens is cached per input content (identical content returns an identical value even when that value is nonsense) and, for content the cache has not seen, roughly 10-60% of requests report a value inflated by a constant ~+170 tokens
endpoint_protocol.neutralisation: every probe carries a fresh 12-hex nonce so no probe can hit the cache; each text is drawn K times with K distinct nonces and the MINIMUM is kept (contamination is one-sided); at least two mutually agreeing uncontaminated draws are required before a text is trusted; the observed spread is reported as an interval; and every endpoint number is cross-checked against an independent real tokenizer
endpoint_protocol.estimator: min(unique-nonce draws of nonce+text) - min(unique-nonce draws of nonce+placeholder) + 1
endpoint_protocol.why_minimum_not_median: the contamination is additive and positive, so the minimum over independent draws estimates the uncontaminated value; the median does not, because contamination can exceed half the draws (5/8 observed in one session), which is recorded here as baseline_contaminated_draws

method.real_tokens_basis: tiktoken:cl100k_base via tiktoken.get_encoding('cl100k_base') succeeded from the local tiktoken cache
method.endpoint_call: POST {api_base}/chat/completions, max_tokens=1, temperature=0, single user message whose content is '[<fresh nonce>] ' + text
method.replay: raw_shell cells: execute_shell_cmd(args['command'], workspace); verseshell_aci cells: execute_aci_op(ACI_OP_MAP[op], args, workspace) then format_aci_result(response, compact=True); one workspace per stored row, calls replayed in recorded order
method.full_text_measurement: chars, utf8_bytes, real_tokens and proxy_tokens are all measured on the FULL observation text; `text` is only a truncated display copy of at most --max-stored-text characters and is never the measurement input; measurement_integrity re-derives that from the stored hashes
method.shape_panel: archetypal observation shapes, always measured, never replayed
method.length_ladder: the same prose at increasing lengths, as a monotonicity check

proxy_tokens.measured_on: the FULL observation text (never the truncated `text` copy)
proxy_tokens.known_error: shape-dependent and two-sided: it under-counts CJK and ASCII JSON/code observations and over-counts plain English prose, so no single correction factor applies

real_tokens.measured_on: the FULL observation text (never the truncated `text` copy)
real_tokens.definition: len(tokenizer.encode(text)) for the observation text the model saw in the stored run, replayed through the real harness functions
real_tokens.reference_tokenizer: cl100k_base (GPT-4/3.5 family, published) — not the vocabulary of the endpoint model
must_not_be_read_as: the endpoint model's own tokenizer (vocabularies differ; see endpoint_cross_check)

endpoint_tokens.measured_on: the same texts, secondarily, under the unique-nonce protocol
endpoint_tokens.definition: min over unique-nonce draws of usage.prompt_tokens minus the nonce baseline; stable only when >= 2 mutually agreeing uncontaminated draws
endpoint_tokens.hazard: content-cached, and intermittently inflated by a constant ~+170 tokens
must_not_be_read_as: ground truth for the text's token count
a pure function of the text

recorded_proxy_tokens.note: the already-published proxy number; kept only for replay fidelity, never recomputed as real tokens

utf8_bytes.why_it_matters: for a byte-level BPE this is the count that bounds real_tokens (real_tokens <= utf8_bytes), unlike the char count

ratio_check.measured_on: cells replayable from the stored run, paired within (task_id, source_run)
ratio_check.note: a recomputed D/A ratio on a replayable subset, not the whole benchmark round; the published_proxy_ratio it carries is a separate historical cohort number and must not be combined with the recomputed values

calibration_anchor.description: fixed ~400-char English paragraph measured every run

length_ladder.note: token counts must grow with text length; the buggy artifact reported 175 tokens for a 12-character text and 178 for a 552-character one

shape_panel.text: A tokenizer turns a string into the sequence of sub-word units the model actually consumes. The proxy used throughout this repository divides the character count by four, which happens to be close for ordinary English prose because the most common words are single tokens and a token averages roughly four characters. That rule of thumb breaks down as soon as the text stops looking like prose: source code spends characters on punctuation and indentation, JSON envelopes spend them on quotes, braces and digests, and Chinese text spends them on characters that are not shared with English. shape_panel.name: cjk_paragraph
shape_panel.text: 这是一个用于校准分词器代理的中文段落。观测文本往往包含中文注释、错误信息以及路径名称，而按字符数除以四来估算词元数量的做法在非 ASCII 文本上会严重低估真实开销。中文汉字通常每个字符需要一个或两个词元，标点符号同样需要词元，因此对于纯中文的观测文本，真实词元数可能达到代理估算值的数倍。这个样本用于量化该偏差，并检验“每四个字符一个词元”是否能作为真实词元数的上界。结论是：不能。对于包含中文的观测文本，该代理是一个下界而非上界。在混合中英文的技术文档中，偏差取决于中文字符所占的比例。建议在报告观测开销时，对非 ASCII 文本单独说明其估算方法。

aggregate.error_direction_detail: ratio = real_tokens/proxy_tokens; a mean ratio < 1 means the proxy OVER-counts (it charges more tokens than the tokenizer does); relative_error = (proxy - real)/real, positive means over-counting. mean ratio=1.5155, median ratio=1.4646, mean relative error=-0.3228.

upper_bound_check.claim: len(text)//4 is an upper bound on real tokens (real <= proxy)

byte_invariant_detail.claim: real_tokens <= utf8_bytes for every measured text
byte_invariant_detail.why_it_must_hold: cl100k_base is a byte-level BPE over UTF-8 bytes: every token emits at least one byte, so real_tokens can never exceed utf8_bytes

chars_bound_observed.claim_as_previously_published: real_tokens <= chars: 'cl100k_base covers at least one character per token, so real <= chars must hold'
chars_bound_observed.why_that_claim_is_false: cl100k_base is a byte-level BPE: a single Unicode character can encode to several UTF-8 bytes and therefore to several tokens, so no tokenizer guarantees one token per character
chars_bound_observed.counterexample_note: the cjk_paragraph sample text itself says the proxy 'is a lower bound, not an upper bound'; that sentence is measured DATA and is kept byte-identical, because changing it would change the documented counterexample. The tool's own prose (build_verdict, this block, the module docstring) states the stronger, correct claim: the proxy is not a bound in either direction.

tokenizer_invariants.note: real_tokens_never_exceed_chars is retained only for backward compatibility and is NOT an invariant; read chars_bound_observed. The invariant that must hold for a byte-level BPE is real_tokens_never_exceed_utf8_bytes.

endpoint_cross_check.note: the endpoint estimate is a SECONDARY, cross-checked number. Where the two disagree beyond the stated tolerance the artifact reports the disagreement and does not pick a winner; the primary tokenizer is the one used for `real_tokens`, the ratios and the D/A check.

verdict.question: is estimate_tokens(text) = max(1, len(text)//4) a defensible proxy, and in which direction and by how much does it err?
verdict.answer: Measured against tiktoken:cl100k_base. the proxy UNDER-counts real tokens on this sample: mean real/proxy = 1.5155 (> 1), i.e. the proxy charges about 32.3% fewer tokens than the tokenizer produces. NO: real > proxy on 52/53 samples (98.1%), i.e. len(text)//4 UNDER-counts real tokens on those shapes ({'ascii_only': 49, 'cjk': 3}). The proxy is NOT a bound in either direction: in this same sample it under-counts 52 and over-counts 1 of 53 scored texts, so no single correction factor converts it into a real-token count. Worst: ascii_only text of 1532 chars scored 525 real tokens against 383 proxy tokens (-27%). no single correction factor exists: across 53 scored texts the proxy under-counts 52, over-counts 1 and exactly matches 0, and the mean real/proxy ratio is shape-dependent (ascii_only=1.5241 (n=50); cjk=1.3723 (n=3)). A per-shape correction — or a real tokenizer — is required; one constant multiplier is not defensible.
verdict.a_error_direction: the proxy UNDER-counts real tokens on this sample: mean real/proxy = 1.5155 (> 1), i.e. the proxy charges about 32.3% fewer tokens than the tokenizer produces
verdict.b_error_magnitude: mean real/proxy = 1.5155, median = 1.4646, mean relative error (proxy-real)/real = -0.3228; proxy over-counts 1 and under-counts 52 of 53 scored samples; the spread is shape-dependent, not a single constant: ascii_only: mean real/proxy=1.5241 (n=50); cjk: mean real/proxy=1.3723 (n=3)
verdict.c_upper_bound: NO: real > proxy on 52/53 samples (98.1%), i.e. len(text)//4 UNDER-counts real tokens on those shapes ({'ascii_only': 49, 'cjk': 3}). The proxy is NOT a bound in either direction: in this same sample it under-counts 52 and over-counts 1 of 53 scored texts, so no single correction factor converts it into a real-token count. Worst: ascii_only text of 1532 chars scored 525 real tokens against 383 proxy tokens (-27%).
verdict.d_cache_hazard_and_neutralisation: The endpoint's usage.prompt_tokens is unusable as written: it is cached per input content (the same text returns the same value even when that value is nonsense), and roughly 10-60% of even cache-missing requests report a value inflated by a constant ~+170 tokens. This tool neutralises both by giving every probe request unique content (a fresh 12-hex nonce), taking K=4 draws and keeping the minimum (the contamination is one-sided, so the minimum is the consistent estimator; a median is not), requiring at least two mutually agreeing uncontaminated draws before a text is trusted, reporting an interval rather than a point, and cross-checking every endpoint number against the independent real tokenizer. 0/0 cross-checked texts were stable.
verdict.e_no_single_correction_factor: no single correction factor exists: across 53 scored texts the proxy under-counts 52, over-counts 1 and exactly matches 0, and the mean real/proxy ratio is shape-dependent (ascii_only=1.5241 (n=50); cjk=1.3723 (n=3)). A per-shape correction — or a real tokenizer — is required; one constant multiplier is not defensible.
verdict.f_tokenizer_byte_invariant: real_tokens <= utf8_bytes holds for 64 checked texts (samples + shape panel) = True, with 0 violation(s). This is the applicable byte-level BPE invariant: every token covers at least one UTF-8 byte.
verdict.g_chars_bound_retracted: The previously published chars bound (real_tokens <= chars) is NOT an invariant and is retracted: it fails on 1 of 64 checked texts, counterexample `cjk_paragraph` (278 chars vs 284 real tokens, 804 UTF-8 bytes). It is kept, explicitly labelled, as tokenizer_invariants.chars_bound_observed (chars_bound_is_not_an_invariant: true).
verdict.h_caliber: a_error_direction/b_error_magnitude/c_upper_bound/e_no_single_correction_factor are about `proxy_tokens` (an OBSERVATION PROXY); f_tokenizer_byte_invariant/g_chars_bound_retracted are about `real_tokens` (a REAL BPE REPLAY on the full text); d_cache_hazard_and_neutralisation is about `endpoint_tokens` (ENDPOINT USAGE). See the top-level `caliber_labels` block; none of these numbers is a cost.

anchor_check.statement: a 400-character English paragraph costs 100 proxy tokens and 89 real tokens (expected [80, 120]); within range: True

published_proxy_ratio_provenance.what_it_is: the historically published D/A observation-token ratio (default 0.8855) computed with the len//4 proxy on the published cohort; its cohort and provenance have NOT been verified against the stored runs
published_proxy_ratio_provenance.must_not_be_combined_with: the current ratio_check numbers in this artifact (totals.real_ratio_D_over_A, totals.proxy_ratio_D_over_A, per_unit): they come from a different, replayable cohort, so averaging, dividing or differencing the two would be comparing unrelated populations
published_proxy_ratio_provenance.interpretation: read it as a historical reference point only; it is not evidence about the current code, and it is not a baseline for the recomputed ratio

ratio_check.unit: (task_id, source_run); cells summed within a unit

sample_scope.note: the recomputed ratio uses only cells that replayed from the stored run AND exist for BOTH conditions inside the same (task_id, source_run) bucket: 53 observations in 8 buckets covering 8 tasks — a subset of the replayable cells (53) and NOT the whole benchmark round (the replay covers only the units selected by --max-units). An unpaired bucket is never merged into another bucket.

direction_agreement.note: direction is which side of 1.0 the D/A ratio falls on INSIDE one (task_id, source_run) bucket; buckets are never mixed, so a disagreement here is a real per-bucket reversal, while the aggregate can also be moved by cell weighting (see sign_flip_robustness)

sign_flip_robustness.note: the aggregate D/A ratio weights cells by their token count, so a few large observations can flip it while most individual units keep the same side of 1.0; this field makes that visible instead of leaving the aggregate to speak alone

ratio_check.conclusion: MATERIAL: the proxy puts the ratio on the other side of 1.0 (real=1.0559, proxy=0.9369); the qualitative conclusion ('D uses fewer observation tokens than A') flips in the aggregate. CAVEAT: 6/8 individual units keep the same side of 1.0, and both aggregate ratios are close to 1.0, so the aggregate flip is driven by cell weighting (a few large observations), not by a per-unit reversal.

caveats: real_tokens is a real tokenizer count (tiktoken:cl100k_base), not the endpoint's usage field. It is the tokenizer of the GPT-4/3.5 family, used here as a published, reproducible BPE reference; the model named in `model` has its own vocabulary, and endpoint_cross_check shows where the two disagree.

the endpoint is a proxy in front of a remote service and is not a pure tokenizer: its usage.prompt_tokens is content-cached and intermittently inflated by ~+170 tokens. endpoint_protocol records the protocol used to neutralise that, and every endpoint number carries its draws, its interval and a stability flag.
endpoint estimates are reported as intervals, never as false-precision point values; the estimator's noise (2-4 tokens) is inherent to the endpoint and is not hidden.

the replayed texts come from one stored live round; commands whose output depends on build state (cargo/pip/tsc) may differ from the stored run, so the proxy/real ratios are representative rather than exact per-cell replays.

the replayed corpus is dominated by short observations, so the aggregate is weighted towards them; aggregate.by_size_bucket and shape_panel show the shape dependence that a single aggregate number hides.

the D/A ratio is recomputed on the same cells with real tokens; it is a statement about this sample, not about the whole benchmark population. Where the aggregate ratio lands on the other side of 1.0 than the proxy, ratio_check.sign_flip_robustness says whether that flip survives at the per-unit level or is produced by cell weighting.

the proxy `len(text)//4` is NOT a bound in either direction and no single correction factor exists: it under-counts CJK and ASCII JSON/code observations and over-counts plain English prose, in the same artifact. A per-shape correction, or a real tokenizer, is required; see verdict.e_no_single_correction_factor.

the earlier `real_tokens <= chars` claim is RETRACTED as an invariant (cl100k_base is a byte-level BPE, so one character can become several tokens). It is kept, explicitly labelled as not an invariant, in aggregate.tokenizer_invariants.chars_bound_observed, with the cjk_paragraph panel counterexample named. The applicable invariant is real_tokens <= utf8_bytes.

ratio_check.published_proxy_ratio_D_over_A (default 0.8855) is a historical published proxy-cohort number whose provenance is unverified: it is NOT the current whole-round baseline and must not be combined with the recomputed ratio_check values, which cover only the cells replayable from the stored run and paired within (task_id, source_run).

every metric carries its caliber: `proxy_tokens` is an observation proxy, `real_tokens` is a real BPE replay of the full text, `endpoint_tokens` is an endpoint usage reading; see the caliber_labels block. None of them is a cost number.
